kurz: Bread is flour, water, salt and a [[triebmittel|raising agent]]. Three processes turn it into a loaf: a [[glutenbildung|gluten]] network, gas from [[fermentation|fermentation]] and a crust from the oven.
bild_im_kopf: Like a balloon in a net: the yeast blows, the gluten holds, the oven sets the shape.
was_passiert: Kneading or resting forms a stretchy gluten network. Yeast or sourdough makes gas that forms bubbles in the network. In the oven the bubbles expand one last time, the starch [[staerkeverkleisterung|gelatinises]] and sets, and the crust browns on the outside.
warum_wichtig: Every bread problem belongs to one of the three processes: network too weak, fermentation off, or oven unfavourable.
faustregeln: Time is the most important ingredient: a long, cool prove gives flavour and structure.
Weigh flour, water and salt; do not measure by volume.
